metas.name: Wag the Dog
metas.description:
A war is invented as a news product. Days before an election, a spin doctor and a Hollywood producer fabricate a conflict with Albania — studio footage, a theme song, a hero — and the media system amplifies it because it fits the format. Made in 1997 with fax-era technology and exact about every mechanism that matters now: the invented event is cheaper, cleaner and more narratable than the real one.

Shortly before an election, a spin-doctor and a Hollywood producer join efforts to fabricate a war in order to cover up a Presidential sex scandal.

metas.name: Sorry to Bother You
metas.description:
Code-switching becomes survival technology. A broke Oakland telemarketer is taught to use his "white voice" and rockets up the company — floor by floor, perk by perk — toward the literal endgame of platform labour, where the worker himself becomes the asset. Boots Riley's satire escalates by following the incentive one step further each time, until the absurdity is just the business model with the lights on.

In an alternate present-day version of Oakland, telemarketer Cassius Green discovers a magical key to professional success--that propels him into a universe of greed.

metas.name: S1m0ne
metas.description:
A synthetic person is preferred by the public to a real one. A producer whose star actress walks out replaces her with Simulation One — a digital performer assembled from the greats — and the forgery becomes the bigger star, demanding interviews, an Oscar, a life. Niccol made it in 2002, before deepfakes, virtual influencers and AI actresses; the satire has spent twenty years quietly becoming a documentary premise.

A producer's film is endangered when his star walks off, so he decides to digitally create an actress to substitute for the star, becoming an overnight sensation that everyone thinks is a real person.

metas.name: Apples
metas.description:
A self is issued by a bureaucracy. An epidemic of sudden, permanent amnesia leaves the unclaimed amnesiacs to a state programme that rebuilds their identities from cassette-tape instructions: ride a bike, eat an apple, jump from a height, record it all on Polaroids. Nikou's deadpan Greek dystopia is about what a person is when their past arrives as a form to complete — memory as paperwork, completed diligently.

Amidst a worldwide pandemic that causes sudden amnesia, middle-aged Aris finds himself enrolled in a recovery program designed to help unclaimed patients build new identities.

metas.name: Dual
metas.description:
Cloning is sold as a consumer service with terms and conditions. Told she is dying, a woman purchases a double to take over her life — trained, delivered, hers — then recovers, and learns the contract's other clause: one of them must be removed, in a court-ordered duel a year later. Stearns shoots every step as a transaction handled by calm professionals; the deadpan is the critique.

A woman opts for a cloning procedure after she receives a terminal diagnosis but when she recovers her attempts to have her clone decommissioned fail, leading to a court-mandated duel to the death.

metas.name: The Pod Generation
metas.description:
A radical change arrives as a corporate benefit. In a near-future New York where natural pregnancy is inefficient, risky and increasingly uninsurable, couples gestate in detachable pods supplied by a tech company — the womb as a managed device with an app, a waiting list and a brand. Softer than a typical dystopia, and exact about the mechanism: nothing is imposed, everything is offered, and the offer is very good.

In a not-so-distant future, tech giant Pegazus offers couples the opportunity to share their pregnancies via detachable artificial wombs or pods. And so begins Rachel and Alvy's wild ride to parenthood in this brave new world.

metas.name: Idiocracy
metas.description:
An ordinary man wakes five hundred years into a future where anti-intellectualism has compounded for generations: crops are watered with sports drink because 'it's what plants crave,' and public language has eroded to slogans. Mike Judge's comedy of drift — an exaggeration whose individual jokes keep quietly coming true.

Corporal Joe Bauers, a decidedly average American, is selected for a top-secret hibernation program but is forgotten and left to awaken to a future so incredibly moronic that he's easily the most intelligent person alive.

metas.name: Sick of Myself
metas.description:
A woman eclipsed by her artist boyfriend takes black-market medication that visibly destroys her face — and converts the damage into fame. The film treats attention as a priced market working exactly as designed: the pathology is not vanity but the exchange rate. A relationship drama with a horror film's logic.

Increasingly overshadowed by her boyfriend's recent rise to fame as a contemporary artist creating sculptures from stolen furniture, Signe hatches a vicious plan to reclaim her rightfully deserved attention within the milieu of Os...

metas.name: BlackBerry
metas.description:
A Canadian startup invents the smartphone era from Waterloo — then loses it to a competitor who understood consumers rather than engineers. Shot like a heist film about keyboards, bandwidth and carrier deals. The useful part is the timing: watching technical superiority stop mattering, quarter by quarter, in real time.

The story of the meteoric rise and catastrophic demise of the world's first smartphone.
